  1800 HUNTINGTON DRIVE

The City of San Marino appreciates your attendance. Citizens’ interest provides the Council with
valuable information regarding issues of the community.

Regular Meetings are held on the 2nd Wednesday of every month at 6:00 p.m. Typically, Adjourned
Meetings are held on the last Friday of every month at 8:30 a.m.

In compliance with the American Disabilities Act, any person with a disability who requires a
reasonable modification or accommodation in order to participate in a meeting should contact the
City Clerk via email at cityclerk@cityofsanmarino.org or by phone at (626) 300-0705 prior to the
meeting for assistance.

  PURSUANT TO ASSEMBLY BILL 361 (AB 361)
Members of the City Council may teleconference into the meeting without noticing each
teleconference location from which a member will be participating in a public meeting.

  CORONAVIRUS DISEASE (COVID-19) ADVISORY
To protect both staff, our constituents, and elected officials, members of the public must follow the
State and County Health Department’s current Health Officer Orders, which require wearing a
mask indoors. Given the seriousness of COVID-19, you are encouraged to provide input
electronically if you do not feel comfortable attending in person.

 TO:  Mayor and City Council

 FROM:  Marcella Marlowe, Ph.D., City Manager
 BY:  Paul Chung, Finance Director
  Mark Siegfried, Accounting Manager/Controller

 DATE:  February 25, 2022
 SUBJECT:  APPROVAL OF AN ANNUAL $100,000 CONTRIBUTION TO THE
  CALIFORNIA EMPLOYERS’ RETIREE BENEFIT TRUST (CERBT)
  FOR FISCAL YEARS 21-22, 22-23, 23-24, AND 24-25

STRATEGIC PLAN CRITICAL SUCCESS FACTORS

• Efficient, Responsive, and Effective City Services
• Fiscally Responsible and Transparent City Government

BACKGROUND

During the February 26, 2021 City Council meeting, the City Council authorized staff to open
the CERBT Section 115 Trust with CalPERS for prefunding Other Post-Employment Benefits
(OPEB) and made a one-time contribution of $500,000. Since funding this program, it has
performed better than expected, yielding an average return of 5.6%, compared to Local Agency
Investment Fund (LAIF), which averaged 0.28% during that same period.

OPEB are benefits, other than pension, that employers provide to their retired employees.
OPEB liabilities arise from an employer’s commitment to contribute to retirees’ healthcare
insurance premiums. Similar to many agencies, the City of San Marino participates in a medical
health plan provided by CalPERS. This plan provides for retiree health benefits to any employee
that retires from the City of San Marino and receives pension benefits. The City currently has
56 retirees that receive OPEB.

DISCUSSION

Staff discussed with the Finance Liaisons and the City Treasurer the continued funding of the
CERBT program and all concurred with recommending an additional $100,000 annual
contribution for the next four years until the Public Safety Parcel Tax expires.
 The benefits of the CERBT program and additional contributions are higher-yielding
investments, reduced unfunded liabilities, improved financial reporting outcomes, and the
benefit of compounding investment growth. CERBT funds can be withdrawn at the City’s
discretion to pay the annual pay-as-you-go retiree medical benefits which are approximately
$200k if cash or liquidity needs are required. The City has full control of the CERBT program.
The additional contribution will provide increased financial leverage yielding higher returns, with
minimal risk, while maintaining the City’s reserve policy per the Citywide Financial Policies.

Staff recommends the City Council reevaluate the annual contribution to the CERBT program
in FY 2025-26 depending upon the outcome of the renewal of the Public Safety Parcel Tax.

FISCAL IMPACT & PROCUREMENT REVIEW

As stated above, if the City Council approves the annual contribution of $100,000 to the
CERBT Section 115 Trust, it will be paid out of the excess cash the City Council could transfer
to the CIP fund. If the City decides to make additional contributions, it would be recorded as
an asset to the City’s financials and it would improve the City’s overall OPEB liability. Future
annual contributions into the CERBT will be included as part of the annual operating budgets.
Furthermore, the status and performance of the Section 115 Trust will be included with the
Quarterly Status Report to City Council.

This report requires no procurement review.

LEGAL REVIEW

The City Attorney’s office has reviewed and approved as to legal form.

RECOMMENDATION

Staff recommends that the City Council approve annual contributions of $100,000 to the
CERBT Section 115 Trust with CalPERS through Fiscal Year 2024-25, for a total of $400,000. If
the Council concurs, the appropriate motion would be:

“I move to make annual contributions of $100,000 to the CERBT Section 115 Trust with
CalPERS through Fiscal Year 2024-25, for a total of $400,000.”

ATTACHMENTS

None.
